title: Capacity healing protocol and postmortem action list for dedicated headroom gap
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: During a production traffic spike on 2025-02-11 we observed a sustained headroom deficit in a subset of Dedicated pools which caused elevated latency for high-throughput customers and triggered an SLO miss. Initial mitigation restored capacity, but the incident exposed an autoscaler regression and insufficient telemetry to detect growing headroom risk before customer impact. This ticket captures the incident timeline, findings, immediate mitigations, and prioritized action items to prevent recurrence.
incident_timeline: 2025-02-11 09:03 UTC - First alert: per-pool available_vcores dropped below configured headroom threshold for pool-dedicated-eu-west-1-3 (observability dashboard alert)
2025-02-11 09:08 UTC - Increased 95th pct latency for hosted endpoints routed to the affected pool; paging started to on-call
2025-02-11 09:15 UTC - On-call (Miguel) verified autoscaler log stream and observed repeated scale-out attempts failing due to spurious API throttles from cloud provider
2025-02-11 09:22 UTC - Emergency manual scale-up applied to pool (add 4 GPU nodes) and fallback routing to secondary pool enabled to protect highest-priority customers
2025-02-11 10:05 UTC - Latency begins to normalize for routed traffic; alerts cleared but post-incident monitoring shows some request rejections for low-priority queues
2025-02-11 11:30 UTC - Triage call: decision to revert autoscaler change deployed 02-09 and backfill missing metric emits as stop-gap
2025-02-12 14:00 UTC - Hotfix deployed (revert + metric backfill) and new runbook steps added for manual headroom augmentation
2025-02-20 10:00 UTC - Draft postmortem completed; engineering review scheduled
Notes: Slack incident channel #inc-2025-02-11-dedicated-capacity remains archived with full logs and play-by-play.
what_we_observed: Autoscaler failed to maintain headroom due to a regression in cooldown logic introduced in PR #1472 which lengthened the effective cooldown window for scale-out under certain request patterns
Critical metric 'pool.pending_scale_errors' was not surfaced as an alerting signal and was absent from runbook troubleshooting steps
Cloud provider API throttling events (quota bursts) caused repeated failed scale attempts; autoscaler retried but the extended cooldown prevented corrective subsequent attempts quickly enough
Fallback routing was configured but not prioritized for medium-priority customers, resulting in partial request rejections rather than graceful degradation
Existing canary for autoscaler changes did not exercise the sustained-burst workload shape that triggered the regression
immediate_mitigations: Applied manual scale-up of affected pools (+4 nodes) to restore headroom (Miguel on-call)
Enabled priority-based fallback routing: high-priority customers rerouted to unaffected pools by updating routing policy 'route-preserve-high-v2'
Rolled back autoscaler cooldown change (revert PR #1472) and deployed a hotfix to restore previous scale-out cadence
Added a temporary alert for 'pool.pending_scale_errors > 5 in 5m' to the SRE alerting group
Updated runbook section 'dedicated/headroom' with precise verification steps and decision thresholds for manual augmentation
root_cause_summary: Primary: Regression in autoscaler cooldown logic that extended the effective cooldown period between successful and attempted scale-outs, introduced by PR #1472.
Contributing: Missing alert surface for failed scale attempts and insufficient telemetry on cloud API throttle responses.
Contributing: Canary tests for autoscaler changes did not reproduce long-lived high qps bursts; test harness needs more realistic traffic shapes.
Contributing: Fallback routing policy had coarse priority rules that did not guarantee graceful degradation for medium-tier customers.
postmortem_action_items: P0 - Restore: Ship autoscaler regression revert to stable branch and add automated rollback on rollout failure - owner: Miguel Santos - due: 2025-02-14 - estimate: 2
P0 - Telemetry: Add 'pool.pending_scale_errors' and 'cloud.api_throttle_rate' as first-class metrics and wire to SLO alerting - owner: Priya Nair - due: 2025-02-21 - estimate: 3
P1 - Runbook: Expand dedicated headroom runbook with exact escalation flow, verification queries, and pre-approved manual scale commands - owner: Ethan Park - due: 2025-02-18 - estimate: 2
P1 - Canary: Create sustained-burst autoscaler canary with 15m+ burst shapes covering QPS and open-connection patterns - owner: Aisha Kapoor - due: 2025-03-07 - estimate: 5
P2 - Routing: Refine priority fallback policy to allow graceful degradation for medium-tier traffic and add tests - owner: Sofia Müller - due: 2025-03-01 - estimate: 3
P2 - Chaos: Add a scheduled chaos test that simulates cloud API throttling during scale operations to ensure autoscaler robustness - owner: Platform Reliability - due: 2025-04-01 - estimate: 5
P3 - Long-term: Design predictive capacity buffer and predictive scaling model that uses traffic trend signals to pre-warm pools - owner: Research Applied ML - due: 2025-06-30 - estimate: 13
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: Revert autoscaler change immediately rather than attempt a partial patch to minimize customer impact (approved in triage call). Trade-off: short-term conservatism vs. delayed feature progress.

Decision: Prioritize telemetry and runbook updates as P0/P1 items since detection and manual remediation time dominated incident impact. Trade-off: delayed investment in predictive scaling feature work.

Decision: For medium-term routing policy changes, we will prefer incremental tests in staging to avoid introducing routing regressions. Trade-off: slightly longer delivery time for routing improvements.

acceptance_criteria: Telemetry: pool.pending_scale_errors and cloud.api_throttle_rate are emitted in every pool and alarmed in SRE on-call
Runbook: dedicated headroom runbook includes exact manual augmentation steps and is referenced in the incident checklist
Canary: sustained-burst canary exists and prevents the autoscaler regression from reaching production in staged rollouts
Routing: fallback routing changes pass integration tests and reduce request rejections for medium-tier traffic in simulated chaos runs
